items.text: The Justice Department filed a federal suit in Alaska on Oct 22 asking that the state be barred from certifying a win by Democrat Mary Peltola over Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) while a same-named candidate, Daniel J. Sullivan, stays on the ballot. On Oct 23 Trump said he told DOJ to file it, and by Oct 24 Democrats and voting-rights groups were challenging it, according to a CNBC headline. Attorney General Todd Blanche said DOJ does not intend to interfere improperly with state certification. A Notre Dame election-law scholar told AP the statute does not let DOJ block certification.
items.reporter: Associated Press; Katherine Faulders et al. (ABC)
items.outlet: AP via Alaska Public Media; ABC News
items.notes: The suit was filed Oct 22, just before the time window, so the news in the window is Trump's admission and the challenge. I could not open the CNBC story about the challenge (fetch failed). Breitbart (Oct 23) framed the suit as defending election integrity and quoted no opposing side. AP and ABC included Democratic criticism and expert doubts. Daniel J. Sullivan won about 2% of the August primary vote. [src:us]

items.text: On Oct 25 a Ninth Circuit panel heard DOJ's emergency bid to make California set aside mail ballots from roughly 20,000 registered voters that federal agencies flagged as likely noncitizens. Live accounts say the panel, including Judges Bennett and Sanchez, doubted it had jurisdiction because the district court had not ruled yet. The judges also questioned whether the Elections Clause lets DOJ tell a state which votes to count. California argues DOJ lacks standing and that the request breaks the NVRA's 90-day rule and the Purcell principle. U.S. District Judge David O. Carter has a hearing set for Tuesday, Oct 27.
items.reporter: Rick Hasen (Election Law Blog); Zachary Fedyk (JURIST)
items.outlet: Election Law Blog; JURIST; CNN; Fox News
items.notes: Hasen's post was written during the argument and marked 'in progress'. I saw CNN's headline (judges skeptical) but could not open the page. Fox News (Sinkewicz/Finn) led with DOJ's claims and those of Bill Essayli, who said noncitizens had very likely already voted in LA County, and put California's objections lower down. Los Angeles County says ballots that have already been processed cannot be traced back to voters. Ninth Circuit case no. 26-7070. [src:us]

items.text: With the Nov 3 midterms about a week away, Trump rallied on Oct 25 in Port Huron, Michigan, for Senate nominee Mike Rogers and gubernatorial nominee John James. Barack Obama campaigned in Detroit on Oct 24 for Democrats Abdul El-Sayed and Jocelyn Benson. Trump attacked El-Sayed on Truth Social, and the Times of Israel reported he said Jews who vote for El-Sayed should be ashamed. The Fox live blog cites Reuters for the current balance: Republicans hold the House 218-214 and the Senate 53-47, so Democrats need a net gain of four seats in each chamber.
items.notes: Most items in the live blog are partisan claims. Speaker Johnson called recent national polls 'wrong' and said they undersample Republicans, and campaign-released internal polls are unverified. I found no independent final-week polling in the window. The most recent independent polls I saw were NYT/Siena in September (Democrats about +9 on the generic ballot among likely voters) and WaPo-Ipsos in July (Democrats +3). Both are stale. Trump's schedule this week: Mississippi on Mon, Texas on Tue, Ohio on Wed (Gray DC). [src:us]

items.text: On Oct 25 Trump told reporters there would be no US strike on Iran that day. That contradicted US envoy Tom Barrack, who had said a weekend strike was possible. Trump also said more strikes before the Nov 3 midterms were possible but that a 'big, beautiful' agreement was too. Iran's President Pezeshkian accused Washington of disrupting talks. The talks are stalled despite a memorandum of understanding signed in June, and the US says it is still enforcing a naval blockade of Iran's ports.
items.outlet: TASS; Times of Israel; ABC News
items.notes: TASS is Russian state media. Times of Israel reported the same Trump remarks about possible strikes or a deal. I found no AP or Reuters text for these remarks (search budget ran out). ABC's live blog (Shalvey/Brennan/El-Bawab) gives background on the stalled MOU and ongoing exchanges of strikes at a lower intensity. [src:us]

items.text: An unclassified Oct 23 memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Iran has substantially increased efforts to target US officials abroad, and a US official confirmed the memo to ABC News. Two senior Iranian officials told the New York Times that US diplomats and personnel are fair targets. The State Department is reportedly cutting staff at embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE and has ordered non-essential staff out of Saudi Arabia.
items.outlet: ABC News; New York Times (via Times of Israel)
items.notes: The memo is confirmed by ABC and reported by the NYT. The embassy drawdowns and the claim that Iran has operatives inside the US come from the NYT as relayed by Times of Israel; I did not see an official State Department notice. UKMTO reported on Oct 23 that a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. [src:us]

items.text: On Oct 23 Trump signed a proclamation that again changes which Canadian goods face the 50% Section 338 duties. The duties were first imposed in July over Canada's motor-vehicle tariffs. Trade-compliance firm GHY says the changes take effect Oct 30. They remove some plywood, paper products, machinery, refrigeration equipment and packing crates, and add some valves, carpets and waste products. This continues a US-Canada tariff escalation that in September added outright import bans on some Canadian goods.
items.notes: I did not see the annex text, so the exact product changes come from GHY's summary. CBP guidance was still pending. On the campaign trail, Mike Rogers said the administration agreed to tariff Canadian trash trucks entering Michigan landfills; this may relate to the added 'waste products' but is unconfirmed. [src:us]

items.text: On Oct 23 CMS proposed a rule requiring ACA Exchanges to verify eligibility before enrollment, implementing the Working Families Tax Cut Act. According to a law-firm summary, the rule would generally bar advance premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions while certain data matches remain unresolved. That could delay or deny subsidies for some marketplace enrollees during open enrollment. The same week HHS kept 2025 civil-penalty levels, and FDA finalized guidance on prescription-drug-use software.
items.outlet: Alston & Bird Health Care Week in Review
items.notes: I could not open the CMS press release or the Federal Register public-inspection PDF (2026-21891) because access was blocked, so the comment deadline and publication date are unverified. [src:us]

items.text: Under its Closer to Zero initiative, FDA issued draft guidance setting action levels for cadmium in processed foods for babies and young children. It also issued a draft chapter on controlling chemical hazards in human food. FDA plans a webinar on Nov 16. Recalls posted Oct 22 include WinCo Foods hoagie rolls (undeclared sesame) and Natural Grocers 2-lb mung beans (possible glass).
items.outlet: AFDO summary of FDA constituent updates
items.notes: This comes from AFDO's digest of FDA's own updates; I did not open the FDA page directly. The comment period for the draft guidance is not stated. [src:us]

items.text: The White House's presidential-actions page lists three Oct 22 actions. One is a proclamation 'Adjusting Imports of Wind Turbines' under Section 232, which follows the Commerce investigation opened in 2025. The second is a Defense Production Act Section 303 determination on domestic petroleum production, refining and logistics. The third is an order titled 'Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People'. Together they point to more tariffs on wind equipment and federal support for oil capacity while the Iran war keeps fuel prices high.
items.notes: These were signed Oct 22, before the window, and could appear in the Federal Register Oct 23-27. I saw only the titles; tariff rates and other details are unverified because I could not open the texts or the Federal Register. [src:us]

items.text: At an Oct 24 rally in Georgia, Trump announced a $4.2 billion Audi factory near Macon expected to create about 4,500 direct jobs. He also repeated his pledge of a $5,000 'Trump dividend' to adult citizens if Republicans hold both chambers, which he estimated would cost about $1 trillion, and warned of a '1929-style' depression under Democratic control.
items.notes: I found no Audi or Georgia state confirmation in the window. The dividend pledge dates from the September RNC convention and is not new. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's FOMC decision is due Oct 28 (see watch). [src:us]

items.text: Alaska Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola and family members were hospitalized with minor injuries after a two-vehicle crash in Anchorage on Oct 24. Her campaign postponed some appearances.
